name: System Time Zone
purpose: Identifies the system's currently configured time zone, needed to correctly interpret event log and other artifact timestamps recorded in local time; System.evtx can supplement this with historical time zone change information.
key_fields: ActiveTimeBias / Bias - offset from UTC in minutes
StandardName / DaylightName - the configured time zone's display names
TimeZoneKeyName - the named time zone (e.g., "Eastern Standard Time")
DynamicDaylightTimeDisabled - whether automatic DST adjustment is disabled
System.evtx Event ID 6013 - logged when the time zone setting changes
normal_baseline: TimeZoneKeyName matches the system's expected physical location or the organization's standard imaging configuration, and remains stable over the system's operational life.
anomalies: A time zone change shortly before or after suspicious activity, which can be used to confuse timeline analysis or make locally recorded timestamps appear to originate from a different region
TimeZoneKeyName inconsistent with the host's known physical location or the organization's standard build
Repeated Event ID 6013 entries in System.evtx indicating multiple time zone changes within a short period
anti_forensic_notes: TimeZoneInformation reflects only the currently configured time zone, not a history of prior changes - that history, when it exists, comes solely from System.evtx Event ID 6013 entries, which are subject to the same log-retention and clearing limits as any other event log.
interpretation: Some log files and artifact timestamps can only be correctly interpreted by knowing the system's time zone. Event ID 6013 in System.evtx can provide additional information on historical time zone settings, supplementing the single current-state value stored in the registry.
